column1: # HX-S-10 — the HCR gate family's per-platform lane manifest.
# For every HCR gate source in the tree, what EACH of the three platform lanes
# does with it. `scripts/check_hcr_lane_manifest.py` holds this table to the
# tree on every `just lint`; `scripts/run_hcr_lane.sh` executes it and refuses
# a result that disagrees with it. Read the former's module docstring for the
# full cell grammar and for why the declaration lives here rather than being
# read out of each gate's own `when defined(...)` guard.
# WHY IT IS A TRACKED FILE AND NOT A DERIVED SET
# Because the failure being prevented is a gate added to ONE platform. A row
# must carry a token for all three columns or lint fails by name, so "added to
# Linux, forgot macOS and Windows" cannot be committed. A derivation from the
# sources could never say that: it would simply agree with whatever the sources
# happen to say, including nothing at all.
# CELL GRAMMAR (summary; the authority is check_hcr_lane_manifest.py)
#   run:<N>              run here, and execute at least N cases, and skip none
#   run:unmeasured       run here; no floor measured on that platform YET
#   run:<N>+skip:<M>     run here; exactly M cases may skip, and each must print
#   unsupported          do not count it here; `--verify-unsupported` runs it
#                        anyway and requires it to execute zero cases
# ONE RULE ABOUT `unsupported` THAT IS WORTH KNOWING BEFORE YOU WRITE IT
# A gate whose SOURCE carries no platform guard is portable by construction,
# and lint refuses to let it be declared `unsupported` anywhere without the
# note token `unsupported-despite-portable: <reason>`. That rule exists because
# the first version of THIS FILE dropped `hcr_rb_application_abi_contract` --
# the platform-neutral rb_hcr_* ABI contract gate, the one deliverable 5 of
# HX-S-10 requires on all three lanes -- from the macOS lane, having read a
# platform guard out of that file's whole-line COMMENT at :21. Nothing would
# have said so: a gate that runs on two lanes instead of three still leaves
#   linux-x86_64   MEASURED 2026-09-19 on Linux 6.12.85 x86_64 in reprobuild's
#                  own dev shell, one `just <target>` per row, `[OK]` markers
#                  counted from test-logs/<target>.log. 41 gates run, 5 declared
#   macos-arm64    NEVER MEASURED. Every `run:` cell is `unmeasured` and says so
#                  rather than carrying a guessed number. The first real macOS
#                  lane run prints the count for each and filling them in is
#                  transcription. Do not write a floor you did not measure.
#   windows-x86_64 NEVER MEASURED, same rule. Note that
#                  is EXPECTED RED — see its note. Turning that red green by
#                  narrowing the row is explicitly out of bounds.
# `rc` is not in this table on purpose: a lane's verdict is about executed cases
# and skips, not about a process exit status. The exit status is what read the
# two bare `skip()` gates as green for their whole lives.
